subject: biology
title: Exchange surfaces and surface area to volume ratio
key_idea: Cells need to take in substances such as oxygen and get rid of waste. Small organisms can do this across their surface. Large organisms have a small **surface area to volume ratio**, so they need exchange surfaces with a large surface area and a transport system.

sections.heading: Why large organisms need exchange surfaces

blocks.text: Every cell must take in substances and remove waste. This section covers why size decides how an organism does it.

items.meaning: The net movement of particles from where they are in high concentration to where they are in low concentration.
A part of the body where substances cross in and out, such as the lungs.
A system, such as the blood, that carries substances between the exchange surface and the cells.

items: Very small, with a **large surface area** compared with their volume.
Short distance from the surface to the middle of the cell.
Diffusion across the cell surface is enough.
Volume increases faster than surface area, so the surface area to volume ratio is **smaller**.
Long distance from the surface to the cells inside.
Diffusion alone would take too long.
So they have exchange surfaces **and** a transport system.
Bigger organism: smaller surface area to volume ratio.
Diffusion alone is too slow over a long distance.
Large organisms need exchange surfaces and a transport system.

sections.heading: Calculating surface area to volume ratio

blocks.text: The ratio compares the surface area with the volume. It is written like 6 : 1, meaning 6 units of surface area for every 1 unit of volume.

blocks.label: Surface area of a cube
where: A cube has six square faces.

items.text: A cube with sides of 2 cm: 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 cm².

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the surface area to volume ratio of a cube. The side length changes each time.
diagram.question: A cube has sides of **{s} cm**. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio. Give your answer in the form ___ : 1.

blocks.text: For a block that is not a cube

blocks.label: Surface area of a block
where: X, Y and Z are the three sides, in cm

blocks.text: Work out the area of each face, add them, then divide by the volume.

diagram.alt: A line graph showing the surface area to volume ratio of a cube falling steeply as the side of the cube increases from 1 cm to 6 cm, then falling more slowly.

items: SA:V = surface area ÷ volume.
As size increases, the ratio decreases.
Small animals have a large ratio. Large animals have a small ratio.

blocks.text: Organisms take in some substances and get rid of others.

rows: Needed by all cells. Plants take it in from the soil
Dissolved food molecules, such as glucose
Needed for healthy growth. Plants take them in from the soil
A waste product made when excess amino acids are broken down. It is carried in the blood to the kidneys and removed in urine

items: In: oxygen, water, food molecules, mineral ions.
Out: carbon dioxide and urea.

blocks.text: Exchange surfaces are adapted so that diffusion is fast. Examples are the alveoli in the lungs, the gills of a fish and the villi in the small intestine.

rows: **Large surface area**, from folds or many small projections
More particles can cross at once
**Good blood supply**, a network of capillaries
Carries substances away, so the concentration gradient stays steep
Brings fresh air or water, so the concentration gradient stays steep

blocks.text: A steep concentration gradient is a big difference in concentration across the surface. The steeper it is, the faster the diffusion.

items: Large surface area, thin walls, good blood supply.
Always link each adaptation to its effect on diffusion.

sections.heading: Investigating the effect of surface area to volume ratio

blocks.text: A common investigation uses jelly cubes of different sizes. The jelly contains an indicator that changes colour when acid reaches it.

items.text: Cut cubes of different sizes and place them in acid.
Measure the time for the colour to change throughout each cube.
Small cubes change faster. They have a larger ratio, so acid diffuses to the middle more quickly.

blocks.label: Rate of colour change
where: time to change colour, in seconds

items.text: A cube takes 132 s. 1 ÷ 132 = 0.0076 per second.

items: Higher surface area to volume ratio gives a faster rate of diffusion.
Rate = 1 ÷ time.

checks.q: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of a cube with sides of 3 cm.
checks.a: Surface area = 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 cm². Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³. Ratio = 54 : 27 = 2 : 1.

checks.q: Explain why a large multicellular organism needs a transport system but a single-celled organism does not.
checks.a: A large organism has a small surface area to volume ratio and a long diffusion distance, so diffusion alone would take too long. A single-celled organism has a large ratio and a short distance, so diffusion is enough.

checks.q: Give three ways an exchange surface is adapted for fast diffusion.
checks.a: A large surface area, thin walls (a short diffusion distance) and a good blood supply to keep a steep concentration gradient.

worked_example.question:
Fish exchange gases through gills. Oxygen from the water enters the blood of a fish through the gills, which have filaments and capillaries.

Explain how gills are adapted to maximise the exchange of oxygen between the water and the blood.
answer_points: The gills and filaments provide a large surface area for diffusion.
A good blood supply, or a network of capillaries, maintains the concentration gradient.
The filaments and capillaries have thin walls, one cell thick, for a short diffusion distance.
The water is in close proximity to the blood supply for a short diffusion distance.
worked_example.tip: Each adaptation scores a mark only when it is linked to its effect on diffusion.

extra.heading: Surface area to volume ratio and heat loss

blocks.text: A warm-blooded animal with a large surface area to volume ratio loses heat faster per unit volume.

items: It needs a greater rate of respiration to release more heat and keep warm.
Respiration is a large part of metabolism, so its metabolic rate is higher.
Small warm-blooded animals therefore have a higher metabolic rate than large ones.

worked_example.question: Explain, using Fick's law, the factors that affect the diffusion rate of molecules into and out of cells.
answer_points: Fick's law: the rate of diffusion is proportional to surface area and concentration difference, and inversely proportional to the thickness of the membrane.
Surface area: as surface area increases, the rate of diffusion increases, because there are more places for diffusion to happen.
Concentration difference: the larger the difference between inside and outside the cell, the faster the rate of diffusion.
Thickness of the membrane: the thicker the membrane, the slower the rate of diffusion, because the diffusion distance is greater.
worked_example.tip: Full marks need all three factors with their effects, and one reference to proportionality.

blocks.text: Fick's law links the rate of diffusion to three factors.

blocks.label: Fick's law
blocks.formula: rate of diffusion ∝ (surface area × concentration difference) ÷ thickness of membrane
where: A bigger surface area or concentration difference speeds diffusion up.
A thicker membrane slows it down.

rows: More places for particles to cross

worked_example.question:
Some students investigate the effect of the surface area : volume ratio on the rate of diffusion in animal cells.

They use hydrochloric acid and gelatine cubes that have been stained blue using a pH indicator solution. The indicator will turn red in acidic conditions.

They put different sized cubes into 3 different test tubes of hydrochloric acid and time how long it takes for the cubes to completely change to red.

The table shows the students' results.

Length of each side of the cube (mm) | surface area : volume ratio | Time to completely change colour (seconds)
2 | | 32
4 | 3 : 2 | 61
6 | 1 : 1 | 170

Calculate the surface area : volume ratio for the cube with sides of 2 mm.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 3 : 1 on the answer line scores both marks. Show 24 : 8 to be safe.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The small intestine absorbs digested food through a very large internal surface area.

items: **Villi** are finger-like projections of the wall of the small intestine.
**Microvilli** are tiny projections on the surface of the cells that cover the villi.
Both increase the surface area, so more digested food is absorbed more quickly.
